pageCache.pageTitle: Old Town Infant School and Nursery - Coastal Learning Partnership
pageCache.text:
Coastal Learning Partnership
Thank you for taking an interest in Old Town Infant School and Nursery, which is a highly valued member of the Multi Academy Trust, Coastal Learning Partnership (CLP).
CLP is a single family of twenty schools across two Local Authority areas: Dorset Council and Bournemouth, Christchurch & Poole Council. The two furthermost points of CLP are Boscombe and Swanage. There are about 5,400 pupils overall who are supported by around 900 committed staff.
Our schools work closely together in a spirit of professional generosity and collaboration, sharing resource and expertise.
Although part of the same single family, every school in CLP is different and unique and those differences are greatly valued. Each school has its own identify and values which express the local communities that they serve. Those schools within CLP which are church schools express their Christian distinctiveness through their unique vision.
CLP’s motto is ‘Broadening Horizons Together’. This is because we want every member of the CLP community to really flourish; children enjoy an inspiring educational experience and staff enjoy professional opportunity and fulfilment. That is achieved through being part of a single learning community.
CLP has three core values which influence the way in which we work together:
Serve: Schools in CLP serve each another as well as their local communities and families
Inspire: Staff inspire each other and their pupils
Empower: Schools, and everyone in them, are empowered to be their very best
Old Town Infant School and Nursery has made a commitment to the CLP family, secure in the knowledge that serving others in this way will lead to a better educational experience for all of the pupils.
If you would like to learn more about the work of the Partnership and its other schools, or to view documentation such as statutory accounts, please visit the Coastal Learning Partnership website.
You can contact Coastal Learning Partnership directly as follows:
Email: office@coastalpartnership.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Old Town Infant School and Nursery - Breakfast Club and After School Club
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club and After School Club
Breakfast Club - 7.30 am to 8.50 am
We are pleased to offer a breakfast club to suit all children.
Early Birds breakfast club runs from 7.30am to 8.15am at a cost of £4. Sessions must be booked via the Arbor app. This is especially useful for parents who need childcare before going to work.
'Best Start' breakfast club runs from 8.18am to 8.45am at no cost to parents, yes, it is FREE! Sessions must be booked in advance via the Arbor app to help us manage food purchases.
This free session is new to Old Town and will allow children to enjoy something to eat in a calm, relaxed environment before the start of the school day. They will have access to some activities such as reading, colouring and puzzles or just chatting with their friends.
Staff will then ensure the children get to their classrooms at 8.50am.
Seashells After School Club - 3.15 pm to 5.00 pm.
Our popular in-house after school provision runs five days per week, term time only.
Children can enjoy a range of activities with snacks and drinks provided.
There are three sessions:
A - 3.15 - 3.45 pm Cost £3
B - 3.15 -4.15 pm cost £6,
C - 3.15 -5 pm cost £10.00,
Sessions MUST be booked in advance online or via the school office (spaces are limited) and payment made via your child's Arbor account.
Reviews – we asked our parents and children for feedback.
'S loves coming to Seashells, it makes it easy for me to be able to work and know she is happy. The staff are fantastic and caring' - Parent year 2 child.
'D loves going to Seashells. If I am early collecting her, she is cross with me as she wants to stay until the end!' - Parent Year 2 child.
'My son loves the football table and Lego blocks. There is a nice atmosphere with children having fun'–Parent Year R child.
'M loves reading the Star Wars books and playing with his friends, there is a wide range of activities, and it is well-structured. Amazing atmosphere, the staff do a great job' - Parent Year 1 child
The children tell us that they like making their own snacks for snack time, the arts and crafts time and the football table is also very popular! They look forward to film night on a Friday when they choose a film.

Governance
Old Town Infant School Local Governing Body
The role of the governing body is a strategic one.
School governors oversee the aims and objectives of the school, and the policies and targets for achieving those aims and objectives. They monitor and evaluate the progress the school is making and act as a source of challenge and support to the headteacher (a critical friend).
Old Town Infant School is part of the Coastal Learning Partnership (CLP) multi-academy trust. For more details about how our Governing Body fits with CLP governance, please see the CLP Financial Regulations Manual and Scheme of Delegation documents (see below). They set out the structure and remit of the members, board of trustees, its committees and local governing bodies. There is more information on the CLP website, including details of CLP trustees and CLP members.

pageCache.pageTitle: Old Town Infant School and Nursery - Sport Premium
pageCache.text:
Sport Premium
What is the PE and Sports Premium Funding?
The Government has provided funding in excess of £150 million per annum to schools to enable them to improve and enhance PE and Sports provision. The funding is being jointly provided for by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport and will see money going directly to primary school headteachers to spend on improving the quality of sport and PE for all their children. The money can only be spent on sport and PE provision in schools.
Possible uses of the funding include:
Hiring specialist PE teachers or qualified sports coaches to work alongside primary teachers when teaching PE
New or additional Change4Life sport clubs
Paying for professional development opportunities in PE/sport
Providing cover to release primary teachers for professional development in PE/sport
Running sport competitions, or increasing participation in the school games
Buying quality assured professional development modules or material for PE/sport
Providing places for pupils on after school sport clubs and residential visits
Improving resources and introducing children to a wide range of physical, social and emotional experiences through sport and PE.
How we will use the funding at Old Town Infant School and Nursery:
Provide cover staff and funding to release teachers for professional development in PE and sport.
Employing specialist sports coaches/teachers to work with all children across the school to ensure a high level of input is available.
Providing professional, specialist sports coaches /teachers to work with all staff across the school to peer coach or model effective techniques so that the quality of sports teaching is strong.
Time devoted to the improvement of PE planning across the school – including the monitoring of its effectiveness.
Promote sport and healthy lifestyles throughout the school in cross curricular areas.
Recognise and reward participation and success.
Increase the sports resources / equipment in school.
Introduce new sports.
Increase the opportunities for pupils to take part in inter and intra school competitions.
Offer PE development and support to Newly Qualified Teachers (NQT).
Enhancing the outdoor space to encourage active participation.
Increase active learning within the classroom.
Promote health and physical fitness to parents.

Pupil Premium
Pupil Premium: Extra Funding for Your Child’s School
Did you know that registering for Pupil Premium means that your child’s school could get extra money?
Pupil Premium is additional funding that the Government gives to mainstream and special schools in England to help children from low income families. The Pupil Premium Grant must be spent to help eligible pupils reach their full potential, both academically and socially, and the school will decide how best to spend this. If you want to know how your child’s school spends the Pupil Premium you can look on their website or ask at the school.

How do I apply for Pupil Premium?
If your child is in Reception, Year 1 or Year 2, you should complete the form "Application for Pupil Premium" available from your child’s school, the Children, Young People and Learning offices in the Dolphin Centre or from the BCP website:
https://online.bcpcouncil.gov.uk/services/freeschoolmeals/ As always, if you have any further questions or queries regarding Pupil Premium, please speak to either the school office, Mrs Brunton or Mr Gubbins. There are also Premiums available to children of Forces Families and Looked After Children. Please let us know if this may apply to your child.

pageCache.pageTitle: Old Town Infant School and Nursery - Hello and Welcome
pageCache.text:
Hello and Welcome
HELLO AND WELCOME TO STARFISH NURSERY!
We would love for your child to join our happy, child-centred nursery where all children are encouraged to reach their full potential and become curious and creative learners within a nurturing and caring learning environment. Our highly qualified and experienced staff are dedicated to the continued development of the children in our care and we know that warm and positive relationships between staff and children, consistent routines and strong relationships with parents are key to providing high quality provision where children feel safe and secure.
Your child really is at the heart of all we do!
At Old Town Infant School, our nursery provision is the start of a child’s learning journey with us, so we are passionate about getting it right! The staff and Governors work together to ensure that we provide a stimulating and supportive learning environment where children can thrive. We recognise, and value, the importance of working with you as parents and carers to support your child in becoming independent, successful and confident learners.
We know that there are lots of things to consider when choosing a nursery for your child and hope that the answers to any questions that you may have will be found in the information tabs below. If you require any further information, or would like to book a visit, please feel free to get in touch. We look forward to hearing from you!
You are welcome to give us a call on 01202 673966 or pop in to the main school office between 8.30am and 3.30pm Monday to Friday, term time only. Alternatively, please drop us an email to: oldtown.nurseryadmissions@coastalpartnership.co.uk
We hope that you and your child will be very happy here in our nursery & we look forward to forming a close partnership with you.
PLEASE NOTE: WE DO NOT OFFER PLACES UNDER THE 9 MONTH AND TWO YEAR OLD FUNDING SCHEMES. OUR NURSERY TAKES CHILDREN AGED 3 AND 4 YEARS.

At Old Town Infant School and Nursery we recognise that for children, high self-esteem, confidence, supportive friends and clear lines of communication with a trusted adult helps prevent the chances of them being abused. Our school will therefore aim to:
